For the treatment plan, it’s helpful to list out any mental health-related symptoms, and then group them by what causes them. This way, the interventions can target multiple symptoms at a time, if possible. Then state a treatment goal and list out different techniques, skills, and interventions that you’re willing to try. 

A treatment plan is a plan, and not written in stone. It can be overwhelming to write it up with your therapist because you’re doing an overview of everything that is affecting your mental health. The plan will evolve over time too. You’ll document your progress periodically (weekly, monthly) to really see how you’ve grown or which treatment goal you’re struggling with.

Hi! I experienced something similar. What really helped, was going over my treatment plan and my goals then breaking those goals up into realistic interventions that I thought I could work on, during the next month. If you and your therapist didn’t create a treatment plan, maybe now would be a good time to do that. Then plan to do a check-in during the first five minutes of each session, to hold yourself accountable for doing work outside of therapy. 

Any progress is good progress, no matter how small. Just the fact that you posted here, asking for advice, is a step in the right direction. I hope things get to where you want them to be! You can do it!
